# Publishes the playable alpha so it can be looked at from any device,
# including a phone that is not on the same network.
#
# Execution stays separate from ci.yml because this workflow ships to the
# public internet. Its trigger is deliberately downstream of a successful CI
# push run, however, so Pages can never publish a main revision that CI has
# rejected. See [L-pages-must-follow-green-ci].
#
# KNOWN LIMIT, recorded because it contradicts TIM-TODO [T18]: GitHub
# Pages cannot set response headers, so it cannot send COOP and COEP.
# Those are required for SharedArrayBuffer, and therefore for WASM
# threads. Nothing needs threads today - the simulation is single
# threaded by design ([D4]) - but [A9] plans parallel systems, and the
# day that lands this host stops being sufficient. Moving is cheap while
# the artifact is a static bundle; it will not get cheaper.

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pages: write
  id-token: write
  # To read which of the triggering CI run's jobs ran.
  actions: read

# One deploy at a time. Cancelling an in-flight run would be wrong here:
# unlike a test run, a half-finished deploy is a state someone might be
# looking at, so let it finish and queue the next. The queue is set on the
# build and deploy jobs rather than the workflow, so an unpublished-docs-only
# run, whose build is skipped, never joins it. GitHub keeps one waiting
# entry per queue and cancels the older one, so a run that joined only to
# deploy nothing could otherwise cancel a waiting deploy of real code.

jobs:
  # Publish game changes and public changelog edits. Other documentation
  # still skips publication. CI compares from the last tested game revision,
  # so a notes-only edit cannot hide code whose own CI never passed.
  decide:
    # `workflow_run` fires for every conclusion, and CI also supports manual
    # dispatch. Only a successful push to main is a releasable revision.
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.event == 'push'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      site: ${{ steps.content.outputs.site }}
    steps:
      - name: Find whether CI tested published content
        id: content
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          RUN: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          tested=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/$RUN/jobs" \
            --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.name == "web") | .conclusion] | any(. == "success")')
          if [ "$tested" = "true" ]; then
            echo "site=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "site=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No published content changed; the site stays as it is."
          fi

  build:
    needs: decide
    if: needs.decide.outputs.site == 'true'
    concurrency:
      group: pages-build
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # A workflow_run starts in the default-branch context. Check out the
      # triggering CI run's tested revision rather than whichever main commit
      # happens to be newest when this runner starts.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}

      # rust-toolchain.toml is the single source for the version,
      # components and targets. See ci.yml for why it is pinned.
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show

      - uses: jetli/wasm-pack-action@v0.4.0
        with:
          version: 'v0.15.0'

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22

      # web/src/wasm/ is gitignored build output, so a fresh clone has
      # none. This must run before the Vite build imports it.
      - name: Build the WASM package
        run: wasm-pack build crates/terri-wasm --target web --out-dir ../../web/src/wasm

      - name: Install web dependencies
        working-directory: web
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build the site
        working-directory: web
        run: npm run build

      # Fail loudly rather than deploying an empty directory. A Pages
      # deploy of nothing succeeds and serves a 404, which reads as a
      # broken URL rather than a broken build.
      - name: Verify the build produced something
        run: |
          set -eu
          test -f web/dist/index.html
          test -f web/dist/changelog/index.html
          wasm=$(find web/dist -name '*.wasm' | head -1)
          test -n "$wasm"
          echo "Game, changelog and $wasm present"
          du -sh web/dist

      - uses: actions/configure-pages@v5
      - uses: actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3
        with:
          path: web/dist

  deploy:
    needs: build
    concurrency:
      group: pages-deploy
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment:
      name: github-pages
      url: ${{ steps.deployment.outputs.page_url }}
    steps:
      # A rerun or overlapping CI run can finish after a newer main run. The
      # concurrency queue orders Pages runs by arrival, not source history, so
      # re-check the live ref immediately before deployment and leave the
      # existing public revision alone when this artifact is stale.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0

      # A tip that differs only in unpublished documentation serves the same
      # site, and its own documentation-only run will not
      # deploy, so the tested revision is still the one to publish. Without
      # this, a documentation push landing during a deploy would leave the
      # game change before it unpublished.
      - name: Confirm the tested revision is still the main tip
        id: release
        env:
          TESTED_SHA: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          current_sha=$(git ls-remote --exit-code origin refs/heads/main | cut -f1)
          test -n "$current_sha"
          if [ "$current_sha" = "$TESTED_SHA" ]; then
            echo "current=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Deploying current main revision $TESTED_SHA"
          else
            git fetch --quiet origin main
            classification=$(python3 -B .github/scripts/changes.py compare "$TESTED_SHA" "$current_sha")
            site=$(printf '%s\n' "$classification" | sed -n 's/^site=//p')
            if [ "$site" = "false" ]; then
              echo "current=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "Deploying $TESTED_SHA; main is $current_sha, which adds only unpublished documentation"
            else
              echo "current=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              echo "Skipping stale revision $TESTED_SHA; current main is $current_sha"
            fi
          fi

      - id: deployment
        if: steps.release.outputs.current == 'true'
        uses: actions/deploy-pages@v4
'
